lessons.title: A New Map
lessons.titleJa: あたらしい ちず

school.topic: 3人称単数の -s：He / She ＋ うごき・has
school.grammar: He has ～. / She likes ～. （I have → he has、I like → she likes）

expressions.ja: ビリモは あたらしい ちずを もっています。

expressions.en: He likes old maps.

expressions.en: Ms. Emma reads the map with us.

testPoints: he / she / ひとの なまえの あとの うごきに s を つけられる（like → likes、have → has）
おわりの s が「ス」と きこえる ことば（likes, eats, jumps, sleeps）を よめる

phonics.tipJa: he / she の ときは うごきに s が つくよ。k・t・p の あとの s は ちいさく「ス」。likes（ライクス）、eats（イーツ）、jumps（ジャンプス）、sleeps（スリープス）。

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Welcome to Stage 2. ステージ2では、わたしは ほとんど えいごで はなすよ。Don't worry. Listen and enjoy! Look, Birimo found something in the library. It's a map! A map of places that are not on any map yet. Wow! Today's sentence is: Birimo has a new map. Say it with me. Birimo has a new map. Great! Listen again. I have a map. But Birimo has a map. When we talk about one person, like he or she, the verb changes. ひとり の ひと の ことを いう ときは、うごきの ことばに s が つくよ。 have は has に なるよ。 I like maps. He likes maps. I eat bread. She eats bread. Can you hear the s? Now, phonics time. Listen to the end of these words: likes, eats, jumps, sleeps. The s is a quiet sound, like a little snake. Sss. Likes. Eats. Jumps. Sleeps. Nice! Our new journey starts today. Let's see the map with Birimo and our friends. Ready? Let's go!

school.topic: 3人称単数の -s：The ship leaves ～. / He plays ～.
school.grammar: The ship leaves at ～. / He plays ～. （もの・ひと ひとつの ときも s）

expressions.en: The ship leaves at seven.
expressions.ja: ふねは 7じに しゅっぱつします。

expressions.en: The captain waves to us.

testPoints: ひとつの もの・ひとりの ひとの ときに うごきに s を つけられる（The ship leaves ～.）
おわりの s が「ズ」と きこえる ことば（plays, runs, swims, reads）を よめる

phonics.tipJa: こえの でる おと（y・n・m・d）の あとの s は「ズ」と にごるよ。plays（プレイズ）、runs（ランズ）、swims（スウィムズ）、reads（リーズ）。のどに てを あてると ふるえるよ。

lessons.teacherScript: Good morning, everyone! Today is a big day. We go to the harbor and get on a big ship. Do you have your ticket? Me too! Today's sentence is: The ship leaves at seven. Say it with me. The ship leaves at seven. Good! The ship is one thing, so we say leaves, with an s. ひとつの もの の ときも、うごきの ことばに s が つくよ。 One more. The captain waves to us. Kiko runs to the ship. Waves. Runs. Can you hear the s? Now, phonics. Yesterday our s was quiet, like sss. Today, listen carefully. Plays. Runs. Swims. Reads. This s sounds like z, zzz, like a bee. ハチの ような「ズ」の おとだよ。 Put your hand on your throat. Say zzz. Can you feel it shake? That's the z sound. Plays. Runs. Great job! Before we go, one tip. On a ship, people say, All aboard! That means, everybody, get on the ship now! Let's say it together. All aboard! Here we go!

phonics.tipJa: 「ス」と「ズ」の くらべっこ。walks・helps は「ス」、sings・rides は「ズ」。まえの おとが いきだけ なら「ス」、こえが でる なら「ズ」だよ。

lessons.teacherScript: Hello again! We're on the ship now. Can you see the blue sea? It's so beautiful. Today, we talk about what our friends like. Today's sentence is: Haru likes the sea. Say it with me. Haru likes the sea. Wonderful! Remember, Haru is one person, so likes has an s. Now listen. I like the sea. Haru likes the sea. Riko loves dolphins. And if you like it, too, you can say, I like the sea, too. ～も すき、と いいたい ときは、さいごに too を つけるよ。 Now, phonics. Let's compare two sounds. Walks. Helps. Those s sounds are quiet. Sss. Sings. Rides. Those s sounds buzz. Zzz. Listen again. Walks, sings. Helps, rides. Can you hear the difference? Try it with me. Walks. Sings. Helps. Rides. Super! Here's a speaking tip. When your friend tells you something, say Me too! or Really? It makes talking fun. Now let's go out on the deck and meet our friends.

lessons.teacherScript: Hi, everyone! We're in our cabin on the ship. Riko has something special. Let's take a look. Today's sentence is: Riko has a notebook. Say it with me. Riko has a notebook. Good! Do you remember? I have, but she has. Let's practice. I have a pencil. She has a pencil. I have a sticker. He has a sticker. Great! Riko writes about the trip every day. It's like a diary. Writes, with an s. Haru wants a notebook, too. Wants, with an s. Now, phonics. Today's words end with s. Listen. Makes. Comes. Wants. Opens. Makes ends with a quiet s. Comes ends with a buzzy z. The e at the end is silent. おわりの e は よまないで、その まえの おとを きいてね。 Say them with me. Makes. Comes. Wants. Opens. Excellent! One more tip. When you want to see something, you can ask, Can I see it? That's very polite. Let's visit Riko's cabin now.

lessons.teacherScript: Land ho! We can see the town! This is Sunrise Harbor. あさひの港町に ついたよ！ The people here are very kind. Let's say hello and introduce our team. phonics.tipJa: sh で おわる うごきは s だけでは いいにくいので es を つけるよ。よみかたは「イズ」。wash → washes（ウォッシズ）、brush → brushes（ブラッシズ）。

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today we're at a little cafe by the harbor. It's cozy, and the hot chocolate is yummy. Our friends brought photos of their families. Let's talk about families! Today's sentence is: My brother plays the guitar. Say it with me. My brother plays the guitar. Nice! Now listen to this one. My mom washes the car on Sundays. Washes. Not washs. Wash ends with s h. After s h, we add e s, and we say iz. sh・ch・x・s で おわる ことばには es を つけて「イズ」と よむよ。 Wash, washes. Brush, brushes. Let's practice the phonics words. Washes. Brushes. Wishes. Pushes. Great! Can you hear the iz at the end? One more thing. When you see a photo, you can ask, Who is this? And your friend can say, This is my sister. Let's try. Who is this? This is my brother. Perfect! Now let's look at the family photos together.

lessons.teacherScript: Hi, everyone! Today we're at a park by the sea. There are a lot of birds here. Look, seagulls! Kiko has a special grandma. Let's hear about her. Today's sentence is: My grandma watches birds. Say it with me. My grandma watches birds. Very nice! Watch ends with c h. So we add e s. Watches. Iz! ch で おわる ときも es を つけるよ。 Here's another one. Teach, teaches. She teaches me their names. Isn't that lovely? And one more. My grandpa goes fishing. Go becomes goes. We'll learn more about goes later. Now, phonics. Repeat after me. Watches. Teaches. Reaches. Touches. Did you hear iz at the end every time? Good listening! Here's a speaking tip. When someone tells you a story, show you're listening. Say, Oh, nice! or That's cool! Your friend will be happy. Now let's sit on the bench and listen to Kiko.

lessons.teacherScript: Good evening, everyone! We're staying at a small inn in the harbor town tonight. But oh no, what's that on the wall? A spider! Birimo is hiding under the blanket. Today's sentence is: He doesn't like spiders. Say it with me. He doesn't like spiders. Good! Listen carefully. He likes cats. He doesn't like spiders. In the second sentence, like has no s. 「～しない」の ときは doesn't を つかって、うしろの うごきには s を つけないよ。 doesn't が s の かわりを してくれるんだ。 He doesn't like. She doesn't have. Birimo doesn't eat green peppers. Now, phonics. Today's words end with x or double s. Fix, fixes. Mix, mixes. Relax, relaxes. Miss, misses. Say them with me. Fixes. Mixes. Relaxes. Misses. Iz, iz, iz! Wonderful! Here's a tip. When you are scared, you can say, Help! And your friend can say, Don't worry. It's okay. Let's help Birimo now!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today we're visiting a cat cafe in the harbor town. There are so many cats! The owner of the cafe is very nice. We want to know about her. How can we ask? Today's sentence is: Does she like cats? Say it with me. Does she like cats? Great! To ask about he or she, start with Does. And look, like has no s. Does she like? Not, does she likes. Does の あとの うごきにも s は つけないよ。 Here are the answers. Yes, she does. No, she doesn't. Let's practice. Does he drink milk? No, he doesn't. Does she have a cat? Yes, she does. Now, phonics. Listen. Dances. Changes. Passes. Buzzes. They all end with iz. Say them with me. Dances. Changes. Passes. Buzzes. Super! A speaking tip for today. When you ask a question, make your voice go up at the end. Does she like cats? Try it. Now let's go inside, quietly. Shh, the kittens are sleeping.

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! It's poster day! We're in the lobby of our inn, and everyone made a family poster. Today you can be a presenter. Today's sentences are: This is my dad. He cooks dinner. Say them with me. This is my dad. He cooks dinner. Excellent! A good presentation has three parts. One, who is it? This is my dad. Two, what does he do? He cooks dinner. Three, something he doesn't do or doesn't like. He doesn't like spiders. だれ・すること・しないこと、の 3つで はっぴょうしよう。 After a presentation, the listeners can ask a question. Does your dad cook every day? Yes, he does. Now, quick phonics review. Three sounds. Cooks, sss. Plays, zzz. Watches, washes, fixes, iz. Wonderful! Remember, look at your friends, speak loudly, and smile. And when your friend finishes, give a big hand! Okay, presenters, are you ready?

phonics.tipJa: y の まえが 子音の ときは、y を i に かえて es。study → studies（スタディーズ）、cry → cries（クライズ）、try → tries、fly → flies。

lessons.teacherScript: Good morning, everyone! It's a new morning at the inn. The sun is rising over Sunrise Harbor. What do you do every morning? Today's sentence is: I always brush my teeth. Say it with me. I always brush my teeth. Good! Always means every time. One hundred percent! Usually means most of the time. always は「いつも」、usually は「たいてい」。 うごきの まえに おくよ。 I always brush my teeth. I usually wash my face first. Now, phonics. Today we learn a new spelling rule. Study. When it's he or she, the y changes to i, and we add e s. Studies. Cry, cries. Try, tries. Fly, flies. y の まえが 子音の ときは、y を i に かえて es だよ。 Say them with me. Studies. Cries. Tries. Flies. Great! Kiko always tries her best. Isn't that nice? Speaking tip. When you ask about someone's morning, ask, What do you do in the morning? Let's get ready together. Toothbrush, ready? Let's go!

lessons.teacherScript: Hi, everyone! Today we're visiting an elementary school in Sunrise Harbor. The children here are friendly. Let's compare our habits with theirs. Today's sentence is: I sometimes forget my hat. Say it with me. I sometimes forget my hat. Good! Here's a list. Always, every time. Usually, most of the time. Often, a lot. Sometimes, now and then. Never, not at all. Zero! never は「ぜったいに しない」。 ゼロ だよ。 I never eat breakfast in bed. He often hurries to school. Now, phonics. Remember yesterday's rule? Y changes to i, and we add e s. Carry, carries. Worry, worries. Copy, copies. Hurry, hurries. Say them with me. Carries. Worries. Copies. Hurries. Wonderful! A speaking tip. When your friend says something about their habits, you can answer, Me too! or Really? I never do that! Let's meet the children now.

lessons.teacherScript: Good morning, everyone! We're having breakfast at the inn. Mmm, this bread is delicious! It's from the bakery next door. The baker is amazing. Guess what time she gets up! Today's sentence is: What time does she get up? Say it with me. What time does she get up? Good! She gets up at four in the morning. Four! That's very early! To ask about a time, say, What time does she, then the verb with no s. What time does he go to bed? What time does she eat lunch? Now, phonics. Some verbs have special forms. Go becomes goes. Do becomes does. Have becomes has. does は「ダズ」と よむよ。 「ドゥーズ」 じゃないよ。 Say them with me. Goes. Does. Has. And remember, study, studies. Great! Speaking tip. When you are surprised, say, Wow! or That's early! Let's ask the baker some questions!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! We're back at the elementary school. It's the end of the day. The bell is ringing. What do the children do after school? lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today is video day! We're going to make a video diary called, A Day in My Life. わたしの 1にち、を ビデオで しょうかいするよ。 Today's sentence is: I usually get up at seven. Say it with me. I usually get up at seven. Good! Let's build our video. Start with the morning. I usually get up at seven. Then add an always sentence. I always eat breakfast with my family. Next, after school. I sometimes play with my friends. Finally, the night. I sometimes read before bed. Four sentences. That's a great video! Use time words, too. Then. After that. At night. Now, a quick phonics review. Gets. Washes. Studies. Goes. Can you hear the different endings? Super! Remember, look at the camera, speak slowly, and smile. Don't say your real address or school name in the video. ビデオでは、じゅうしょや がっこうの なまえは いわないでね。 Okay, camera on. Action!

lessons.teacherScript: Good morning, everyone! It's very early. Look, the sun is rising! We're at the fishing port, and the fishing boats are coming back. Today we learn how to talk about jobs. Today's sentence is: What does he do? Say it with me. What does he do? Good! Be careful. What does he do? doesn't mean, what is he doing now. It means, what's his job? What does he do? は「いま なにを している？」 では なく「おしごとは なに？」 だよ。 Answer like this. He's a fisher. He catches fish every morning. She drives a boat. Now, phonics. Listen to the end of catch. Catch. It sounds like ch, but we write t c h. After a short vowel, we use t c h. Catch. Match. Watch. Kitchen. Say them with me. Catch. Match. Watch. Kitchen. Excellent! A speaking tip. When you meet someone at work, you can say, Your job looks fun! or That's cool! Let's watch the fishers at work.

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Do you remember the baker? She gets up at four. Today we're helping at her bakery! Put on your apron. Today's sentence is: She works at the bakery. Say it with me. She works at the bakery. Good! To ask about a workplace, say, Where does she work? She works at the bakery. Where does he work? He works at the post office. はたらく ばしょ は works at の あとに いうよ。 And when a customer comes in, the workers say, Can I help you? That's a friendly way to say, hello, what do you need? Now, phonics. More t c h words! Fetch. Sketch. Stretch. Ketchup. Say them with me. Fetch. Sketch. Stretch. Ketchup. Great! After a short e, we write t c h, too. One more tip. When you get something, say, Thank you! And when someone says thank you, say, You're welcome! Okay, bakers, let's get to work!

lessons.teacherScript: Hi, everyone! Bang, bang, bang! What's that sound? We're at the shipyard. A shipyard is a place for making and fixing boats. Today we meet a man who fixes boats. Today's sentence is: He fixes boats. Say it with me. He fixes boats. Good! Remember, fix ends with x. So we say fixes, with iz. He uses a hammer and a big brush. Uses also ends with iz. Let's try a question. Does he make boats? No, he doesn't. He fixes them. Them means the boats. them は「それらを」。 ここでは ふねの ことだよ。 Now, phonics. More t c h words. Switch. Patch. Scratch. Stitch. Say them with me. Switch. Patch. Scratch. Stitch. Wonderful! Here's a tip. When you don't know a word, ask, What's this? or What's this called? People are happy to teach you. Let's go inside the shipyard. Be careful, okay?

Pitch. Itch. Witch. Great! Speaking tip. In a busy place, people talk fast. If you don't understand, it's okay. You can say, Sorry? We'll practice that soon. Now, let's be job detectives at the fish market!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, reporters! Today, you are all news reporters. We will interview the people of Sunrise Harbor about their jobs. Microphones ready? Today's sentence is: What do you do every day? Say it with me. What do you do every day? Good! In an interview, we talk to the person, so we say you. What do you do every day? I check the lighthouse lamp every night. Do you like your job? Yes, I love it! Then, we report to our friends. He checks the lamp every night. He loves his job. インタビューでは you、ほうこくする ときは he や she に かえるよ。 Now, phonics review. Catch and teach. Both have the ch sound. But catch has a short a, so we write t c h. Teach has a long e sound, so we write c h. Kitchen, lunch, sketch. Say them with me. Catch. Kitchen. Teach. Lunch. Sketch. Excellent! At the end, always say, Thank you for your time! Let's start the interviews!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today we're under the big lighthouse. A local girl is here. She's very friendly. Let's practice real conversation! When you listen to a friend, don't be quiet like a stone. Give a reaction! はなしを きく ときは、あいづちを うとう。 Today's sentence is: Really? Me too! Say it with me. Really? Me too! Great! If your friend says, I like soccer, and you like soccer, too, say, Really? Me too! If something is new to you, say, Oh, I see. And if you both don't like something, say, Me neither. I don't like rainy days. Me neither. Now, phonics. New spelling! Listen. Bridge. Badge. Edge. Hedge. The sound is j, but we write d g e. After a short vowel, we use d g e. Say them with me. Bridge. Badge. Edge. Hedge. Wonderful! One more tip. Smile and nod when you listen. Your friend will want to talk more. Let's go and say hi!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! We're in the harbor plaza. There's a fountain and kids are playing ball. Yesterday we learned reactions. Today, let's learn how to keep a conversation going. Here's the secret. After you talk about yourself, ask the same question back! じぶんの ことを いったら、おなじ しつもんを あいてに かえそう。 Today's sentence is: I like soccer. How about you? Say it with me. I like soccer. How about you? Very good! How about you? means, what do you think? What do you like? What about you? means the same thing. Let's practice. I'm from Japan. What about you? I like dogs. How about you? Now, phonics. More d g e words. Judge. Fudge. Lodge. Dodge. Say them with me. Judge. Fudge. Lodge. Dodge. Great! Another tip. Conversation is like playing catch. You throw a question, your friend throws it back. Let's play ball in the plaza. Ready? How about you?

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, music lovers! Tonight there's a small concert at the harbor. Can you hear the drums? Boom, boom! Today, let's learn how to ask for more details. Sometimes a friend says, I like music. That's nice, but music is a big word. So ask, What kind? くわしく ききたい ときは What kind? 「どんな？」 と きこう。 Today's sentence is: What kind of music do you like? Say it with me. What kind of music do you like? Good! What kind of food do you like? What kind of books do you like? I like books. What kind? Funny books! Now, phonics. Here are more d g e words. Wedge. Ledge. Ridge. Gadget. In gadget, d g e is in the middle. Say them with me. Wedge. Ledge. Ridge. Gadget. Super! Speaking tip. Your friend will be happy when you ask a second question. It shows you are interested. Let's enjoy the concert and ask our friends some questions.

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Whoa, it's so windy today! We're on the pier, and the wind is very loud. Sometimes we can't hear our friends. Sometimes people talk too fast. What should we do? Don't just say yes! Ask again. ききとれない ときは、わかった ふりを しないで、ききかえそう。 それは はずかしい ことじゃ ないよ。 Today's sentence is: Sorry? Can you say that again? Say it with me. Sorry? Can you say that again? Excellent! And if it's too fast, say, Can you speak more slowly, please? When you understand, say, Oh, I got it. Thank you! Let's try. Blah blah blah! Sorry? Can you say that again? Perfect! Now, phonics. Find d g e in these words. Fridge. Badger. Hedgehog. Porridge. Say them with me. Fridge. Badger. Hedgehog. Porridge. Great! Remember, good speakers ask again. It's a strong skill. Let's walk to the end of the pier. Hold your hat!

lessons.teacherScript: Good evening, everyone! Tomorrow is the harbor festival. Tonight, everyone is hanging up lanterns. It's beautiful! Some local kids are here. It's chat time! Let's use all our conversation skills. Number one, react. Really? Me too! That's cool! Number two, ask a second question. What kind? Number three, ask back. How about you? Number four, if you don't understand, ask again. Sorry? 4つの わざを ぜんぶ つかって、ながく はなそう。 Today's sentence is: That's cool! What kind? Say it with me. That's cool! What kind? Great! Now, phonics review. Listen. Bridge, badge. After a short vowel, d g e. Page, huge, large. After a long vowel or a consonant, just g e. Say them with me. Bridge. Badge. Page. Huge. Large. Excellent! Here's my last tip. Try to talk for a long time. Six turns or more! If you forget a word, that's okay. Smile and keep going. Let's sit in a circle and chat.

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, quiz fans! Welcome to Harbor Quiz Time! We're at the top of the lighthouse. We met so many people in Sunrise Harbor. The fisher, the baker, the boat fixer, the lighthouse keeper. Let's see if you remember them. Today's sentence is: Does he work at the lighthouse? Say it with me. Does he work at the lighthouse? Good! Here's how the game works. I think of a person. You ask yes or no questions with Does he or Does she. Does she work at the bakery? Yes, she does! Does he fix boats? No, he doesn't. He catches fish. クイズの こたえは Yes か No。 Does で きいてね。 When you know the answer, say, Is it the baker? Now, phonics review. Listen to the endings. Works. Rides. Fixes. Washes. Sss, zzz, iz, iz. Wonderful! Quiz tip. Listen carefully to every hint. Ready? Hands on your buzzers. Let's play!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! We're on the ship again, sailing around the harbor. The sea is calm today. Today, let's talk about our friends' days. You know a lot about Riko, Haru, Kiko, and Birimo now. Today's sentences are: Riko gets up at six. She reads every morning. Say them with me. Riko gets up at six. She reads every morning. Very good! Remember, when we talk about a friend, the verb gets an s. Gets. Reads. And use frequency words. She always has a notebook in her bag. Haru never goes to bed early! Riko is an early bird. She gets up early. Haru is a night owl. He stays up late. early bird は はやおきの ひと、 night owl は よふかしの ひと。 Now, phonics review. Studies. Goes. Has. Reads. Say them with me. Studies. Goes. Has. Reads. Great job! Speaking tip. Use and, then, and after that to connect your sentences. Let's talk about our friends!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! We're at the post office in Sunrise Harbor. Let's write postcards to our families! A postcard is short. Just three sentences is great. Today's sentence is: This town has a big lighthouse. Say it with me. This town has a big lighthouse. Good! Here's how to write a postcard. Start with Dear and the person. Dear Mom. Then write three sentences. One, about the town. This town has a big lighthouse. Two, about the people. The people here get up very early. Three, about you. I love the fish here! End with, See you soon! and your name. Dear で はじめて、3文 かいて、さいごに じぶんの なまえ。 It's easy! Now, phonics review. Sketch. Catch. Bridge. Badge. Say them with me. Sketch. Catch. Bridge. Badge. When you write these words, don't forget the t and the d! Writing tip. Start every sentence with a capital letter and end with a period. Let's get our pens!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! This is our last walk in Sunrise Harbor. Let's walk along the beach and remember all the people we met. Today's sentences are: She likes cats. He works at the shipyard. Say them with me. She likes cats. He works at the shipyard. Excellent! Let's remember more. The baker gets up at four. She doesn't sleep late. The fisher catches fish. He doesn't fix boats. The cat cafe owner has twelve cats. Does she like cats? Yes, she does! You can say so many things now. 3人称単数の s、doesn't、Does ～?、ぜんぶ つかえるように なったね。 Now, phonics review. Match, beach. Fridge, page. Remember the rule. After a short vowel, t c h and d g e. Say them with me. Match. Beach. Fridge. Page. Wonderful! Speaking tip. When you leave a place, you can say, We'll miss you! It means, we will feel sad without you. Let's say goodbye to our friends in the town.
